title: Welcome!
text:
Welcome!
I’m Monique, a current graduate student pursuining a Master in Environmental Data Science at the Bren School of Environmental Science and Managment located within the University of California Santa Barbara (UCSB). Besides my interest to advocate for environmental justice, I enjoy discovering new vegan restaurants, practicing my non-primary languages (Spanish, French, and Korean), and learning new skills, such as djing, filmmaking, and (of course) coding! To learn more check out my about me or browse through my past projects.

title: Master of Environmental Data Science

Documentary on Environmental Veganism
Below is my research-based documentary:




For my Critical Thinking course (ES 40), we were tasked to do a research project of our choice and interest throughout the entire quarter. My question was based on the small percentage of students in my environmental classes identifying as vegan or vegetarian despite studies showing the amount of water and land usage that is put into upholding the meat and dairy industry. Thus, did veganism matter in the overall context of helping the Earth, if those who studied it did not partake in it?
In this documentary, you’ll find:

Student interviews
Resources to combat food insecurity
Free weekly community dinner
A tour of a co-op housing focused on a plant-based diet

title: Master of Environmental Data Science
section: A personal data collection and an interactive plot
text:
A personal data collection and an interactive plot
For a final project, we had to build an interactive plot using data we collected over the quarter. I chose to collect the dates and time I practiced yoga and the pain levels I experienced throughtout the week in terms of if I practived or not. This was a simple data collection, but was still great to use to become familiar with the R language.
Code below:

library(tidyverse)
library()
library(janitor)
library(htmlwidgets)


mydata <- read.csv("Data.csv") |>
  clean_names() |>
  mutate(
    tooltip_text = paste0(
      "Yoga Session: ", did_you_do_yoga, "<br>",
      "Pain Level After: ", pain_level_after)
  )

p <- ggplot(mydata, aes(
  x = did_you_do_yoga,
  y = pain_level_after,
  color = pain_level_after,
  text = tooltip_text
)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 2.5, alpha = 0.6) +
  stat_summary(geom = "point", fun = mean, color = "#4a4a4a", size = 3) +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "#f9f871", high = "#7c3f98") +  # yellow to purple gradient
  labs(
    x = "Did You Do Yoga?",
    y = "Pain Level After Yoga",
    color = "Pain Level"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#ffe6eb", color = NA),        # baby pink background
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#ffffff", color = "#ffb6c1"), # white panel with pink border
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "#ffccd5"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

plotly::ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text") |>
  plotly::layout(hoverlabel = list(font = list(size = 14)))

title: Monique Allyson Hernandez

My Adventures around the world
The coolest thing to me when I was a kid was the idea of seeing the entire world, which is something I wanted to have my own child experience along with me. My family have origins from multiple parts of the world, including Mexico, South Korea, Portugal, and Spain.
My bucket list of places to visit has grown larger and larger as time goes on, but there are two places that are dear to me that take precedence. One is the birth place of my mom which is Jalisco, Mexico and the other is Seoul, South Korea where my paternal grandmother originates, though she was also born in Yucatan, Mexico.












France Trip 2022.

My favorite traveling memory is taking my 1 year old son to Europe and having him tag along everywhere we went like a 15 pound backpack! We stayed in Lyon, France and visited Paris as well as Geneva, Switzerland. His first playground he played on was a french playground and they really set the standard for playgrounds after that. Even more recently, we visited Tulum, Mexico where we spent all day at the pool or at the beach. And of course, no matter the location, my favorite thing to do is eat the local vegan food.

title: Monique Allyson Hernandez
text:
My Vegan Lifestyle



Homemade and Restaurant


I wasn’t born into a vegan life; I adopted one. I have always had a great interest in reducing my meat intake, cutting out dairy for health reasons, and just not harming animals in general, but never took the plunge until 2022.
People may think it’s just changing the diet, but it’s other things too like not buying fur, wool, or leather. My vegan lifestyle blends very well with my academic interests and I have had the chance to explore environmental veganism due to my major. There are many challenges that come with being vegan as the food may not be so easily accessible such as animal-based food, but with time and experience those challenges have become minimal. There are so many great dishes that have found their way into rotation. Currently, there’s a tuscan gnoochi dish that is comforting, filling, and delicious, but the best part is that it’s incredibly fast!

title: Suitable locations for potential aquaculture
text:
Marine aquaculture have the potential to be a more sustainable option than the alternative land-based meat for the global food supply (Hall et al, 2011). Gentry et al. created a map based on the neccessay constraints for marine aquaculture including, ship traffics, dissolved oxygen, and bottom depth, concluding that the global seafood demand could be met with less than 0.015% of the global ocean area.
The main goal is to create a function that will input the following: minimum and maximum sea surface temp, minimum and maximum depth, and the species name. The output will be a map of the EEZ regions colored by the amount of suitable areas for the selected species.
Which Exclusive Economic Zones (EEZ) is suitable for aquaculture?
The approach to find suitable locations will be determined based on the range of suitable sea surface temperature (SST) and depth values for the species, both oysters and blue mussels.

Which Exclusive Economic Zones (EEZ) on the West Coast is suitable for aquaculture?
Which Exclusive Economic Zones (EEZ) on the West Coast of the US are best suited to develope marine aquaculture for several species of oysters and a species of your choice. Suitable locations will be determined based on range of suitable sea surface temperature (SST) and depth values for the species.

Gentry et al. created a map based on the neccessay constraints for marine aquaculture including, ship traffics, dissolved oxygen, and bottom depth, concluding that the global seafood demand could be met with less than 0.015% of the global ocean area.
Which Exclusive Economic Zones (EEZ) on the West Coast of the US are best suited to develope marine aquaculture for several species of oysters and a species of your choice. Suitable locations will be determined based on range of suitable sea surface temperature (SST) and depth values for the species.

title: Suitable locations for potential aquaculture
text:
Workflow for Oysters


Show code
# variables for min and max
min_sst <- 11
max_sst <- 30

# Reclassifying SST and depth data into suitable locations
# SST reclassification matrix
  rcl_sst <- matrix(
    c(
      -Inf, min_sst, 0,
      min_sst, max_sst, 1,
      max_sst, Inf, 0
    ),
    ncol = 3,
    byrow = TRUE
  )

min_depth <- 0
max_depth <- -70

# Depth reclassification matrix
rcl_depth <- matrix(
    c(
      -Inf, max_depth, 0, # should max_depth be negative?
      max_depth, min_depth, 1,
      min_depth, Inf, 0
    ),
    ncol = 3,
    byrow = TRUE
  )



Find Suitable Zones for Oysters


Show code
# reclassify sst and depth to suitable zones
zone_sst <- classify(sst_mean_c, rcl = rcl_sst)

zone_depth <- classify(resampled_depth, rcl = rcl_depth)

# Combine to adhere to satisfy both sst and depth for suitable zones
depth_sst_zones <- c(zone_sst, zone_depth)




Show code
# Find suitable zones for oysters adhering to both conditions
suitable_zones <- lapp(depth_sst_zones,
 function(sst_data, depth_data) sst_data * depth_data)




Find suitable total area inside EEZ


Show code
# Converting sst data to match suitable zones
sf::st_crs(eez_data)<- terra::crs(suitable_zones)




Show code
# Convert to raster
eez_raster <- rasterize(eez_data, suitable_zones, field = "rgn_id")




Show code
# Calculate cell size
cell_size <- cellSize(suitable_zones, unit = "km", mask = TRUE)




Show code
# Use only the cells with value 1 as suitable in the total area
suitable_zmask <- mask(cell_size,suitable_zones, maskvalues = 0)




Show code
# Select raster cells by suitable zpmes inside EEZ
desired_zone <- zonal(suitable_zmask,eez_raster, fun = 'sum', na.rm = TRUE)




Create Map for Oyster Colored by EEZ Regions


Show code
# Create tibble
z_tibble <- as_tibble(desired_zone)

# Merge for desired zones to EEZ data
map_1 <- left_join(eez_data, z_tibble, by = "rgn_id")




Show code
# Creating a color palette to differentiate the regions
color_palette <- c("#d0f0f0", "#5fb3c7", "#1f78a8", "#08306b")




Show code
# Visualize oyster suitable area by EEZ region
tm_basemap("OpenStreetMap") +
  tm_shape(map_1) +
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "area",
    fill_alpha = 0.7,
    col = "grey30",
    fill.scale = tm_scale_continuous(values = color_palette),
    fill.legend = tm_legend(
      title = "Suitable Area (km²)",
      position = tm_pos_out("right", "center")
    )
  ) +
  tm_text(text = "rgn_key", size = 0.7, col = "grey20") +
  tm_compass(type = "8star",
        size = 2, position = c("right", "top")) +
  tm_scalebar(position = c("left", "bottom"), size = 5) +
  tm_options(component.autoscale = FALSE) +
  tm_title("Suitable Oyster Aquaculture\nin the West Coast by EEZ", size = 1)

ℹ Please use 'text.size' instead.


Warning: The scale bar would be 1.3 times as large when plotted at the top and 1.1 times
as large when plotted at the center











Numerical Oyster Reprsentation within EEZ Regions


Show code
# Create a table for area by region and suitability
map_1 |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(rgn_id, area, area_km2) |>
  arrange(desc(area)) |>
  mutate(pct_suitable = area / area_km2 * 100) |>
  kable(
    digits = 1,
    col.names = c(
      "EEZ Region",
      " Suitable Area (km²)",
      "Total EEZ Area (km²)",
      "Suitable (%)"
    ),
    caption = "Oyster Aquaculture by Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) in the West Coast",
    booktabs = TRUE
  ) |>
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position"))

text:
EEZ Species Function: Blue Mussel
Utilizing the function created above, a map, as well as a table with the total suitable area depicted numerically, can be easily recreated for the desired blue mussel rather than recreate the lengthy process of manually inputing the inforamtion for sea surface temperature and depth.
The function is called after EEZ species and used as shown:

eez_species(min_sst, max_sst, min_depth, max_depth, species_name)

Simply Input into the funtion:

Oysters:

min_sst = 11°C
max_sst = 30°C
min_depth = 0 meters
max_depth = -70 meters
Species_name = Oysters

Blue mussels:

min_sst = 5°C
max_sst = 20°C
min_depth = 0 meters
max_depth = -60 meter
species_name = Blue Mussel

Output:

map of EEZ regions colored by amount of suitable area

# Verify function by using oysters
oyster <- eez_species(11, 30, 0, -70, 'Oysters')

title: Suitable locations for potential aquaculture
section: The importance of aquaculture and sustainability
text:
The importance of aquaculture and sustainability
A recent study from the UN shows that aquaculture can improve food security and nutrition by increasing the amount of seafood available for people to eat. If done correctly, aquaculture increases food production, boosts economic growth in coastal and rural areas, and can help keep waterways clean.

title: Suitable locations for potential aquaculture
text:
Analysis
Blue mussels are eurythermal and well adapted to temperatures of 5–20 °C, with an upper thermal tolerance limit of about 29 °C for adults (Matoo et al., 2021).
For the oysters, the information is the following:

Oysters:

Sea surface temperature: 11-30°C
Depth: 0-70 meters below sea level

Blue mussel:

Name: Mytilus edulis
Sea surface temperature: 5-20°C
Depth: 0-60 m

title: Suitable locations for potential aquaculture
text:
Conclusion
Using the Exclusive Economic Zones to map out suitable areas for marine species that have a high potential for aquaculture development in the west coast of the United States.
The conditions for the species were determined by using the sea surface temperature and depth below, oyster with a range of 11-30°C and maximum depth of 70 meters below sea level, and blue mussels with a range of 5-20°C and a maximum depth of 60 meters.
The area for oyster farming was found to be in Central California with a total of 4,373.6 km^2 and the lower bound being in Northern California with 323.9 km^2.
As for the second species, the suitable location being in Washington with a total of 6545.8 km^2 and the lowest being in Northern California with a total of 2410.1 km^2.
